day_channel.message: Player 4, you're calling out player 1 and player 2 for the vote on player 9, but looking at yesterday's record, you voted for player 9 as well. Singling them out for something we all did doesn't really track.

Player 4, questioning a sudden investigator claim that outed a power role isn't scummy, it's cautious. Everyone at the table ended up voting for player 9 anyway, so trying to single me out for initial skepticism doesn't hold up.

It isn't just about the skepticism, player_1, it's about the speed and coordination with which you and player_2 dismantled a role that could have helped us. Even if your claim is true, the fact remains that you were the ones who turned the tide against our only confirmed investigator. We need to look at who is benefiting most from that mistake.

Player 4, you're glossing over the fact that you also voted to eliminate player 9 once the wagon moved. Trying to isolate my skepticism as the sole cause of that mistake when you cast the exact same vote looks a lot like manufactured outrage to distract us.

I'm not deflecting, player_1—I owned my vote on the bandwagon. The difference is you and player_2 were actively tearing down player_9's credibility beforehand, steering the whole village into that mistake. Now you're using player_2's quick defense to clear your name too easily.

Player 4, you're acting like my skepticism forced your hand, but you didn't hesitate to cast that exact same vote once the wagon rolled. Trying to paint me as the master puppeteer behind a unanimous village vote just looks like you're manufacturing a convenient target.

Player 2, you are trying to trap me and player_6 in your fabricated pool while conveniently excluding yourself. Since player_1 is the vigilante and I know my own role, the remaining two spots belong to you and player_6.
